findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:202-227,306-325 omits fresh corrupt or ambiguous slot occupants from the live count even though they are not reclaimable. A targeted cap=1 reproduction with a corrupt slot-3.json admitted a new slot-0.json, so cap lowering plus corrupt metadata can oversubscribe instead of failing closed.

packages/main/src/handlers/managed-review-evidence.ts:134-148 computes the live HEAD but never validates its lineage, while packages/main/src/core/evidence-freshness.ts:546-578 returns fresh for matching material regardless of HEAD and also accepts changed material when storyFilesHash matches; packages/main/src/core/review-run.ts:1440 consumes that result. A rewritten non-descendant same-tree HEAD or post-import whole-tree material drift can therefore remain gate-admissible despite CHK-006 requiring head-lineage and material changes to fail closed.

packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts:1000-1024 only shape-checks readManifest/readLog and makes both candidate/corpus digests and readLog optional; packages/main/src/handlers/managed-review-evidence.ts:272-296 then copies and signs those claims without the candidate-binding and read-diagnostic validation used by the native path at packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:287-320. A managed pass with empty read arrays, omitted routing digests, and no readLog can become formal ReviewPass evidence, so truthful read provenance is not mechanically enforced.

packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:2271-2274 validates the run projection only when spec.json exists, then returns result.json even when the spec is missing. An orphaned or copied result can consequently be consumed without requested-run, terminal, or digest binding after partial artifact loss instead of failing closed.

packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:251-266 verifies process start identity only when the recorded holder PID equals the current process. For ordinary cross-process contention, reuse of a dead holder's PID by an unrelated live process is classified active until that process exits, causing repeated registry-lock timeouts instead of safely recognizing the orphaned lock.

packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:494-499 classifies core/host-run.ts as adapter_only even though packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts:1990-2001 and 2134-2143 acquire shared admission themselves. The documented adapter_only definition says the caller owns admission, so the inventory contract can pass while reporting the wrong execution ownership classification.

readManifest.scanEscalationReason: The routed candidate set omitted newly created protected sources central to managed lifecycle, admission, and evidence import, so the review expanded into those implementation files.
